newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares surge, seen extending gains Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares surge, seen extending gains Monday.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the fifth session running and analysts said Friday's 5.2-percent surge accompanied by higher turnover and strong buying after price fixing signalled another gain on Monday.
They said foreign investors were apparently buying on a bourse which had begun to look cheap compared with neighbouring exchanges such as Hungary's hitting all-time highs this month.

"I think it's attractive compared with other emerging markets in the region, the market in local currency terms really hasn't gone anywhere this year," said Geoffrey Skipper, chief strategist at Poland's Korona mutual fund.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 5.2 percent to 16,759.7 points and turnover rose 48.4 percent to 304.7 million zlotys ($87.4 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 106 to 0 with four stocks flat.
Banks continued to outperform the surging overall market this week after having underperformed it earlier in the year.
Of the 14 main-market stocks rising at least nine percent on Friday seven were banks: Handlowy, Gdanski, Slaski, PPABAnk, Amerbank, BRE and PBR.
